findings.issue: The event data (admin, offset 96, offset 32 * n1 + 128, n1, tokens1, n2, tokens2 in memory order) is printed with the second array's length and elements inside the first Array(...) and the second head offset after it, so a reader cannot match it to (admin, address[], address[]); text_check agrees with execution, so only the presentation is wrong.
findings.rule: When log or return data is a standard ABI encoding of several dynamic values, print it as the decoded tuple (admin, Array(n1, ...), Array(n2, ...)); otherwise print its words in memory order without nesting one array inside another.
findings.verified: text_check run --per-selector 16: 0 differences, 17 calls with events

notes: No loop in the source. The 12 whiles are the validated ABI encodings of the address[] calldata parameters, once into the constructor arguments of the deployed registry (after the creation code copied from code.data) and once into the event data ('require cd[s] == address(cd[s]); mem[t] = address(cd[s])'); they are implicit and readable. The three single-address deployers (deployAddAllowedRecipient, deployRemoveAllowedRecipient, deployTopUpAllowedRecipients) are simple creates with constructor arguments and events; all faithful.
summary: Faithful factory text without source loops; its loops are validated ABI encodings, and the deployment event's data with two dynamic arrays is printed in a misleading nested form.
